# Interleaved revision comparison

Persistent baseline and current workers run serially as balanced ABBA/BAAB quartets with identical fixed iterations, warmups, runtime, CPU affinity, encoding policy, inputs and JPEG hashes. Startup and IPC are outside encode timing. Ratios below1 favor current. Allocations are mean bytes per encode; retained rental capacity and peak working memory are separate measurements.

MAD, repeated-leg drift, p90/p10 minority-state drift and order bias guard the timing evidence. Invalid rows retain raw measurements and cannot support a speed claim. Valid rows remain inconclusive unless every quartet differs by more than 0.5% in the same direction. This comparison has no native parity verdict.

Release comparison: 256/256 cases against published 1.0.0 source `a40868bfdace7d737413085522a88d351aa16782`, rebuilt with the candidate SDK. 0 valid cases consistently favor 1.0.0 and fail the regression gate. Invalid or missing evidence fails validation separately. Inconclusive differences are retained and do not prove equal performance. The gate checks latency; allocation counts are reported separately.

Timing-only instability permits at most 8 complete attempts per case. The first valid attempt is final, including regressions and inconclusive results; the fastest trial is never selected. Identity, JPEG, structure, nonfinite and too-short failures are never retried. Samples are never merged or removed within a trial. 3 cases were initially invalid; 3 were retried. Every earlier invalid trial remains below and in separate raw files; selected results do not describe an initially stable matrix. Conditioning on stability can favor quieter intervals, including intervals without GC, so the selected trials do not characterize the full latency distribution of all attempts.
